dir=\"ltr\">Michael Moynihan enters his 14th season in Evanston in 2025, where he has earned five NCAA Tournament berths and coached the 2016 Big Ten Champion team. Moynihan's all-time record with the program is 126-109-39, making him the winningest coach in school history. His five NCAA Tournament Appearances account for all but two of Northwestern's appearances all-time.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nDuring his first season with the Wildcats, Moynihan guided the program to a five-win improvement from the previous year, including a three-match Big Ten winning streak to close the season. He reached the 200-win milestone in Northwestern's 2012 finale, a 1-0 shutout of Michigan State in East Lansing.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nNorthwestern racked up ranked wins in 2014, taking down No. 16 Notre Dame, No. 15 Marquette, No. 19 Illinois, No. 14 Rutgers, and No. 6 Penn State. The team earned a 9-8-4 record overall, with over half of its wins coming against ranked opponents.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn 2015, Moynihan led Northwestern to its first NCAA Tournament since 1998. That squad broke a plethora of school records, including most Big Ten wins (seven) and fewest goals allowed in a season (15). Junior Addie Steiner was named to the All-Big Ten 2nd Team, and senior captain Nandi Mehta won the Sportsmanship Award.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nMoynihan led NU to the NCAA Tournament for the second-straight year in 2016. The squad's Sweet Sixteen run marked just the second appearance for the 'Cats in program history and the first since 1998. Northwestern finished the season 16-3-4 overall to tie the renowned 1998 team for most wins in a single season. The Wildcats did not lose a single match against a team ranked outside the RPI top 22 (based on the end of season RPI data).\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nThe Wildcats tournament bid was bolstered by the stalwart play of the NU defense. Lauren Clem, the first NSCAA All-American in program history, anchored a backline that saw a team-best and NCAA-leading 17 shutouts as well as a goals-against-average of .290 to lead the country.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn addition, Moynihan and his staff produced a program-best six All-Big Ten honorees in 2016, including the program's first-ever Big Ten Goalkeeper of the Year, \u003Ca href=\"http://nusports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4870\">Lauren Clem\u003C/a>. Sophomore \u003Ca href=\"http://nusports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4891\">Kayla Sharples\u003C/a> joined Clem for her first All-Big Ten First Team honor and sophomore \u003Ca href=\"http://nusports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4894\">Marisa Viggiano\u003C/a> was named to the All-Big Ten Second Team, while fifth-year senior \u003Ca href=\"http://nusports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4886\">Nandi Mehta\u003C/a> and junior \u003Ca href=\"http://nusports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4875\">Kassidy Gorman\u003C/a> were recognized on the All-Big Ten Third Team. Mehta was also recognized as the Big Ten Sportsmanship Award honoree. \u003Ca href=\"http://nusports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4897\">Maddy Lucas\u003C/a> was named to the Big Ten All-Freshman Team.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn 2017, the Wildcats finished the season with a record of 12-8-3 under Moynihan. The squad made it to the championship round of the Big Ten tournament before losing to Penn State in the finals. Following the championship run, Northwestern made it to the Round of 32 in the NCAA Tournament before falling to UCLA. Four women earned Big Ten honors, with juniors Kayla Sharples and Marisa Viggiano being named to the All-Big Ten First Team, junior Hannah Davidson making the All-Big Ten Third Team, and freshman Regan Steigleder being named to the All-Freshman team. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nMoynihan led the Wildcats to a record of 10-5-4 in the 2018 campaign. They made it to the NCAA tournament for the fourth straight year, losing in the first round to NC State. The ‘Cats earned four All-Big Ten picks under his tutelage throughout the season. Seniors Kayla Sharples and Marisa Viggiano earned All-Big Ten First Team, senior Brenna Lovera earned All-Big Ten Second Team, and freshman Mackenzie Wood earned Big Ten All-Freshman Team. Senior Aspyn Repp also earned the Big Ten Sportsmanship Award.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nMoynihan’s teams at Northwestern have excelled academically, with 209 players earning Academic All-Big Ten honors. In 2016, Nandi Mehta was named a CoSIDA first-team Academic All American, and an NSCAA Scholar second-team All-Region, while Lauren Clem was named an NSCAA Scholar First-Team All-American.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nPicked to finish 11th in the Big Ten in the 2022 Big Ten Preseason Coaches Poll, Moynihan led the Wildcats to a dream season, tying program records with 16 wins and an NCAA Tournament Sweet Sixteen appearance. After a banner regular season that saw a program-record 13-game unbeaten streak and conference-high eight All-Big Ten honorees, NU earned a No. 4-seed in the NCAA Tournament, the best seed in school history. NU dispatched SIUE 3-0 in the First Round and Vanderbilt 2-1 in the Second Round before bowing out at eventual National Champion UCLA.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn 2023, Moynihan claimed his 300th career win with a 7-0 rout of Oakland on August 24, 2023, with 107 of those wins coming at Northwestern.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nPrior to his arrival at Northwestern in December of 2011, Moynihan coached 19 years with the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee women's soccer program, where he led the Panthers to nine NCAA Tournament appearances, 13 Horizon League Championships and eight Horizon League Tournament titles. Moynihan, an eight-time Horizon League Coach of the Year, coached the Panthers to 12-straight conference titles.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn 15 years as the head coach at Milwaukee, Moynihan accumulated a 193-84-38 record, including an 86-8-5 (.894) mark in Horizon League games. In 2011, Moynihan's Panthers won a school-record 19 matches, including a perfect 8-0-0 record in conference action, and advanced to the NCAA Tournament second round. Led by nine all-conference honorees, including the Horizon League Player of the Year, Defensive Co-Player of the Year and an NSCAA All-American, the Panthers finished the season ranked No. 23 by the National Soccer Coaches Association of American (NSCAA) with a final RPI of No. 25.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nThe Milwaukee, Wis., native's coaching career began with the Panthers in 1993 when he served as an assistant coach under his sister, Susan. He helped guide the Panthers in that capacity to a 40-33-4 mark in four seasons, laying the groundwork for when he would take over the program in 1997. Michael also played an instrumental role in fundraising efforts to have the Panthers' home field, the Laura Moynihan Field, named after his mother who also coached the UWM women's soccer program.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nAn active member of the Milwaukee community, Moynihan served on the board of directors for the Shorewood Kickers and was the director of coaching for the Wisconsin Girls Olympic Development Program. At UWM, his teams regularly hosted soccer camps and clinics throughout the area.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nMoynihan played collegiately at Wisconsin, graduating in 1990 with a degree in history. While at Wisconsin, Moynihan was a four-year letter winner, served two years as team captain and received the team's Bill Reddan Award for Sportsmanship as a senior. He also earned a teaching certificate in secondary education from UWM in 1993.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nMoynihan holds a USSF`A' coaching license as well as a USSF national youth license. He has been heavily involved in the Olympic Development Program for the past 20 years, coaching at the national, regional and state levels and has served as head coach for the `93 Wisconsin state team and as an assistant with the `95 regional team.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cstrong>Moynihan Year-by-Year Head Coaching History\u003C/strong>\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Ctable border=\"0\" id=\"docs-internal-guid-65ad92e6-7fff-c4e8-ccd4-65177492db30\">\u003C/span>\u003Cspan id=\"docs-internal-guid-65ad92e6-7fff-c4e8-ccd4-65177492db30\">Rich Manning joined the Wildcats as an assistant coach in June 2021 after\u003C/span>\u003Cspan id=\"docs-internal-guid-789a959b-7fff-959c-9588-2d7708b1b7ce\"> previously serving as the head coach at Utah for 19 years. In Salt Lake City, he led the Utes to eight NCAA Tournament appearances and five Mountain West championships. He also was associate head coach at Santa Clara when the Broncos captured the national title in 2001. \u003C/span>\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nDuring Manning's second season in Evanston, the Wildcats broke a number of program records en route to an NCAA Tournament Third Round appearance. After a banner regular season that saw a program-record 13-game unbeaten streak and conference-high eight All-Big Ten honorees, NU earned a No. 4-seed in the NCAA Tournament, the best seed in school history. NU dispatched SIUE 3-0 in the First Round and Vanderbilt 2-1 in the Second Round before bowing out at eventual National Champion UCLA.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nOver Manning's four years at Northwestern, NU has earned 15 All-Big Ten selections and 12 United Soccer Coaches All-Region honorees, including 2022 Big Ten Freshman of the Year, Caterina Regazzoni.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cspan id=\"docs-internal-guid-789a959b-7fff-959c-9588-2d7708b1b7ce\">“We are excited to have Rich join our Wildcat family,” said Moynihan. “As it is with everyone we bring into our family, we look closely at each person’s core values. All enjoyment, fulfillment, and success stem from having the right team culture and we are obsessed with getting that right.\"\u003C/span>\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cspan id=\"docs-internal-guid-789a959b-7fff-959c-9588-2d7708b1b7ce\">“Several things stand out right away when you meet Rich,” Moynihan continued. “He is a warm and compassionate human being and he has an optimistic outlook on life that is both refreshing and energizing. He is also curious and a life-long learner that has a true passion for soccer. As a former teacher, he excels at creating constructive and productive learning environments and he invests in the development of the whole person. Combining these qualities with Rich’s vast experience at both the NCAA Division I and Power Five conference levels, and the work ethic he has displayed in guiding his teams, he will be an excellent fit for our program and our Wildcat family. We can’t wait to get started working with him.”\u003C/span>\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cspan id=\"docs-internal-guid-789a959b-7fff-959c-9588-2d7708b1b7ce\">At Utah, Manning guided his team into the NCAA tournament in 2002, 2003, 2004, 2005, 2006, 2013, 2016, and 2019, with a program-best run into the NCAA Third Round in 2016, where the Utes fell to eventual national champions USC. \u003C/span>\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cspan id=\"docs-internal-guid-789a959b-7fff-959c-9588-2d7708b1b7ce\">Manning also won three Mountain West Conference regular season championships in 2003, 2005 and 2006 while also claiming two conference tournament titles in 2003 and 2004. After Utah joined the Pac-12 in 2011, Manning’s teams posted four Top-5 finishes in the standings in one of the best conferences in the country, home of five of the last 10 national champions. \u003C/span>\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cspan id=\"docs-internal-guid-789a959b-7fff-959c-9588-2d7708b1b7ce\">During his tenure at Utah, Manning posted a 192-144-53 overall record, including a 77-67-24 record against conference opponents. As an assistant and eventual associate head coach at Santa Clara, the Broncos posted an 84-11-2 record and won three West Coast Conference championships.\u003C/span>\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cspan id=\"docs-internal-guid-789a959b-7fff-959c-9588-2d7708b1b7ce\">Manning mentored 27 NSCAA All-Regional players and one All-American at Utah as well as 54 all-conference selections including 24 first-team honorees. He has also coached three conference offensive players of the year, two defensive players of the year and three freshmen of the year. \u003C/span>\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cspan id=\"docs-internal-guid-789a959b-7fff-959c-9588-2d7708b1b7ce\">At Utah, Manning recruited 15 United States youth international players and posted seven elite recruiting classes in 2003, 2004, 2007, 2011, 2016, 2018 and 2020. Manning was the head recruiter during his stint at Santa Clara and posted three Top-10 nationally ranked classes in four years, including a class that ranked No. 1 overall. Manning recruited and coached nine players that went on to play with the U.S. National Team, including two national players of the  year in Mandy Clemens and Aly Wagner. \u003C/span>\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cspan id=\"docs-internal-guid-789a959b-7fff-959c-9588-2d7708b1b7ce\">Manning also spent the fall of 2020 as an assistant coach with the Utah Royals during the NWSL fall series. He worked with established national team veterans Amy Rodriguez, as well as U23 USA internationals Tziarra King and Gaby Vincent.\u003C/span>\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cspan id=\"docs-internal-guid-789a959b-7fff-959c-9588-2d7708b1b7ce\">In the classroom, Manning led Utah to an NSCAA Team Academic Award every season since 2009 – the longest streak of any Pac-12 team. Since joining the Pac-12 in 2011, Utah women’s soccer posted 111 all-academic selections from the conference. Manning also coached five NSCAA Scholar All-Americans and 18 All-Region honorees.\u003C/span>\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cspan id=\"docs-internal-guid-789a959b-7fff-959c-9588-2d7708b1b7ce\">Prior to joining the Santa Clara staff, Manning worked with numerous youth programs in Southern California. From 1994-97, he was head coach at Los Alamitos High School, where he produced two CIF championships and sent eight players to NCAA Division I programs. Manning took 1996 CIF Coach of the Year honors and was named the 1997 Orange County Coach of the Year.\u003C/span>\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cspan id=\"docs-internal-guid-789a959b-7fff-959c-9588-2d7708b1b7ce\">Along with his success at Los Alamitos, Manning helped develop the S.C. Blues soccer club in San Juan Capistrano, Calif., into one of the nation’s top girls’ youth programs.\u003C/span>\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cspan id=\"docs-internal-guid-789a959b-7fff-959c-9588-2d7708b1b7ce\">Manning played at Santa Clara from 1982-1986 under former U.S. National Team coaches Steve Sampson and Ralph Perez. As a senior, Manning was captain of the Broncos. He earned All-Far West accolades as a junior. Manning graduated from Santa Clara cum laude with a B.S. in mathematics in 1986, followed by a master’s in education from Azusa Pacific in 1996.\u003C/span>",{"mediaCaption":15,"url":3935,"absoluteUrl":3936,"altText":3937,"title":3937,"creditName":15},"/images/2025/8/8/AC_Manning.jpg","https://nusports.com/images/2025/8/8/AC_Manning.jpg","Rich Manning",{"staff_title":3910,"staff_email":3911,"staff_phone":3912},{"abbrev":305,"shortDisplay":305,"shortName":307,"globalSportId":240,"globalSportNameSlug":308,"globalSportGender":248,"id":309,"title":114},3636,"Assistant Coach","Rich","Manning",8574,[3946,3949,3950,3951,3952,3953,3954,3955,3956,3957],{"platformName":613,"userName":3947,"url":3948,"icon":3140,"oldIcon":15},"@CoachManning","https://twitter.com/CoachManning",{"platformName":620,"userName":15,"url":15,"icon":3142,"oldIcon":3143},{"platformName":607,"userName":15,"url":15,"icon":3145,"oldIcon":3146},{"platformName":2222,"userName":15,"url":15,"icon":3148,"oldIcon":3149},{"platformName":3151,"userName":15,"url":15,"icon":3152,"oldIcon":3153},{"platformName":3155,"userName":15,"url":15,"icon":3156,"oldIcon":3157},{"platformName":3159,"userName":15,"url":15,"icon":3160,"oldIcon":3161},{"platformName":3163,"userName":15,"url":15,"icon":3164,"oldIcon":3165},{"platformName":3167,"userName":15,"url":15,"icon":3168,"oldIcon":3169},{"platformName":3078,"userName":15,"url":15,"icon":3171,"oldIcon":3172},{"bio":3959,"twitter":21,"image":3960,"images":15,"displayFields":3964,"sport":3965,"latestCoachBioId":3966,"latestSupportBioId":15,"latestBioId":3966,"id":3966,"title":3941,"firstName":3967,"lastName":3968,"email":3918,"phone":21,"url":15,"staffId":3969,"socialMediaR":3970,"custom1":21,"custom2":21,"custom3":21,"custom4":21},"A Goshen, N.Y. native, Duval comes to Northwestern from Robert Morris, where she served as the first assistant and goalkeepers coach. In her lone season with RMU, Duval led the Colonials to many program firsts. The Colonials earned their second-straight top four conference finish, hosted a Horizon League Tournament Quarterfinal match for the second-straight year–defeating IU Indy, advanced to the Horizon League Tournament Semifinals for the second time in as many seasons, all program firsts.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nDuval's goalkeeping unit posted five shutouts, a 1.58 goals against average, and a .764 save percentage. Graduate student goalkeeper Brenna Murray was named to the 2024 Horizon League All-Tournament Team, received the 2024 Horizon League Women's Soccer Sportsmanship Award, received the Horizon League Sportsmanship Award for all sports, and earned a prestigious NCAA Postgraduate Internship for the 2025-2026 cohort. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn addition to her duties at RMU, Duval is a Goalkeeper Academy coach for the ECNL Pittsburgh Riverhounds Development Academy. This past summer, Duval had the opportunity to work for the Pittsburgh Riveters as the assistant goalkeeper coach in their inaugural season of the USL-W League. The Riveters currently sit atop the table and are in position to win the Great Forest Division. Last summer, Duval was the Assistant Goalkeeper Coach for the Greenville Liberty in the USL-W League, located in Greenville, S.C. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nPrior to Duval's arrival in Moon Township, she served as the graduate assistant goalkeepers coach at Lenoir-Rhyne (N.C.). In 2023, the Bears clinched the South Atlantic Conference Regular Season Championship, the South Atlantic Conference Tournament Championship, as well as the NCAA Southeast Regional Championship. Her goalkeeping unit posted 12 clean sheets, a .81 goals against average, and a .756 save percentage. Duval and the rest of the Lenoir-Rhyne staff earned United Soccer Coaches Southeast Regional Staff of the Year honors.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nAs a student-athlete, Duval attended Campbell, where she appeared in 38 matches, tallying seven shutouts, recording a 1.13 goals against average and a .765 save percentage. During her junior season, the Camels won the 2020-21 Big South Tournament Championship, earning the league's automatic bid into the 2021 NCAA Women's Soccer Tournament. In her senior season, the Camels claimed the 2021 Big South Regular Season Champions. Duval wrapped up her career with one final season at D'Youville University (N.Y.), where she was named a United States Collegiate Athletic Association Second-Team All-American.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nDuval received her Bachelor of Science in Exercise and Sports Science from Campbell University in 2022 while graduating Cum Laude. In May 2025, Duval also graduated with her Master of Arts in Organizational Leadership from Lenoir-Rhyne University. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nCurrently, Duval holds a USSF D License and a United Soccer Coaches Advanced National Goalkeeping Diploma. She will be looking to pursue both her USSF C Field Player and USSF C Goalkeeping Licenses in the near future.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\"We are thrilled to add Reaghan to our staff,\" head coach Michael Moynihan said. \"She will be working closely with our goalkeepers and they will benefit from her passion for the position as well as her own experience as a college athlete. She has already completed the highest levels of licensing for coaching goalkeepers in the U.S. and brings a wealth of knowledge. We have a very talented group of goalkeepers and I look forward to seeing them develop under her guidance. Beyond goalkeeping, it became clear to us very quickly that Reaghan shares the same values we focus on in our program. She will be a great role model for all of our student athletes and she will help bring out the best in everyone around Andy Walsh joined Northwestern Sport Psychology Services in August 2022 as the Postdoctoral Fellow in Sport Psychology. Dr. Walsh provides mental health and mental performance services for Northwestern student-athletes and teams, working collaboratively with Sports Medicine and coaching staffs to optimize student-athletes’ well-being. Prior to becoming a postdoctoral fellow, during the 2021-22 academic year Dr. Walsh worked at Northwestern University’s Counseling and Psychological Services as a Doctoral Intern in Psychology. He is a Certified Mental Performance Consultant® through the Association of Applied Sport Psychology. Prior to his current work with Northwestern student-athletes, Dr. Walsh provided mental health and mental performance services to NCAA Division I and III athletic teams, as well as youth, college, and elite-level athletes and professionals.
